forcedChoices.choice: Peter and Jesus speak to each other with «tú»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish rule: one person to one person uses tú; the Master is a teacher, not a ruler or judge.

forcedChoices.choice: Jesus speaks to the apostles with «ustedes»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish rule: plural you is ustedes.

forcedChoices.choice: Opening » at the start of the continued speech
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish marks a quote that continues into a new paragraph with ».
English 'you' can be John or all; Jesus answers John's question, so the singular fits the context best.

forcedChoices.choice: «el fragmento de su Padre que mora dentro»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish needs a possessive; 'su' keeps 'his Father' open as in the English, and 'que mora dentro' does not add a named person.
